case_title: The Student Who Cannot Stop Being Sick
correct_diagnosis: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in new-onset type 1 diabetes mellitus
questions_asked: How long have you been vomiting today?
Did your flatmate have a stomach bug — did hers get better quickly?
Before the vomiting started, were you very thirsty or drinking a lot?
Have you been urinating more than usual, even at night?
Any weight loss over the past few weeks?
Is your breathing fast or deep — has anyone noticed?
Any fruity or sweet smell on your breath?
Where exactly is the abdominal pain?
Have you been able to keep any fluids down?
diagnosis_submitted: iabetic ketoacidosis — new onset type 1 diabetes

evidence: Did your flatmate have a stomach bug — did hers get better quickly?

premature_closure.reason: No premature closure detected — thorough workup completed.

feedback_given: Your diagnosis of diabetic ketoacidosis is spot on, particularly given the patient's symptoms of vomiting, abdominal pain, and deep breathing.
To confirm the severity of the patient's condition, it would have been crucial to assess her vital signs, including blood pressure and temperature.
Measuring blood glucose levels through a capillary sample would have also been essential to support your diagnosis and guide initial management.
Additionally, an arterial blood gas would have helped assess the patient's acid-base status and guided further treatment.
